questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: In an experiment testing if fertiliser amount affects plant height, keeping water the same for all plants, what is the controlled variable?
questions.why: The controlled variable is whatever is deliberately kept the same so it can't affect the result — here, that's the water. Fertiliser is the independent variable (what's changed) and plant height is the dependent variable (what's measured).

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: Order these events from root cause to final consequence
questions.why: The chain starts with the root cause (poor harvests) and ends with the final consequence (anger at the government) — each step causes the next.

questions.subject: Music
questions.prompt: In song structure, what is the term for a section that gives a song's main theme, repeated with the same melody and lyrics each time?
questions.why: The chorus repeats with the same melody and lyrics each time and carries the song's main theme; a bridge contrasts by introducing new material instead of repeating.

questions.subject: Science
questions.prompt: What term describes a wave caused by the sudden movement of the sea floor during an underwater earthquake?
questions.why: A tsunami is a giant sea wave triggered by sudden movement of the sea floor, most often during an underwater earthquake.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 84°. What is the alternate angle on the other line?
questions.why: Alternate angles are equal — they sit on opposite sides of the transversal between the parallel lines, so the answer is 84°.

questions.subject: Maths
questions.prompt: A triangle has two angles of 40° each. What is the size of the third angle?
questions.why: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°. 180 − 40 − 40 = 100°, so this is an obtuse triangle (one angle over 90°), not an acute one — don't assume equal base angles mean a small third angle.

questions.subject: English
questions.prompt: In the Romeo and Juliet prologue, what does the Chorus say the two families share?
questions.why: The prologue opens by describing the Montagues and Capulets as sharing an 'ancient grudge', setting up the feud that drives the whole play.

questions.subject: History
questions.prompt: A historian says 'the plague caused the labour shortage, and the labour shortage caused peasants to demand higher wages.' Explain why it matters to separate these two links in the chain rather than treating the whole event as one single cause.
